intro_html: The Olive Garden favorite, rebuilt at home: golden chicken strips, bell peppers, and red onion over spaghetti in a garlic butter sauce. Each bowl carries 60 grams of protein at 871 calories for about $4.03 (at everyday cost). The restaurant version is mostly butter and pasta anyway, and those are two of the cheapest things you can buy.
cost_closing_html: About $4.03 a bowl (at everyday cost) for chicken scampi that would run you $16 to $18 with breadsticks and a tip at the chain that made it famous. Fourteen bowls for the price of two restaurant plates is the whole argument.
shop_smart: Six pounds of chicken breast for $13.66 is the anchor here. Club packs at about $2.23 a pound are the play; small grocery trays can run nearly double.
Store-brand spaghetti covers 36 ounces for $2.19. Pasta is one of the last places in the store where a name brand buys you almost nothing.
One pound of butter at $3.06 makes the entire sauce rich. Compare that to a $6 jar of alfredo that would cover half the batch.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Boil the spaghetti 1 minute short of package time, drain, and toss with a spoonful of oil so it does not clump.
Slice the chicken into strips, season with salt and pepper, and dredge in the flour. Sear in batches in vegetable oil until golden and cooked through to 165 F. Set aside.
In the same pot, saute the sliced green and red bell peppers with the red and yellow onion until they soften with a little char, about 5 minutes. Set aside with the chicken.
Melt the butter, add the garlic and red pepper flakes, and cook 1 minute. Sprinkle in a couple spoonfuls of the leftover dredging flour and whisk 1 minute more.
Whisk in the chicken broth and lemon juice and simmer until the sauce thickens enough to coat a spoon. Stir in the parsley.
Return the chicken, peppers, and onions, then toss with the spaghetti and half the parmesan.
Portion into 14 containers and top with the remaining parmesan.
portion_html: Weigh the loaded pot, subtract the empty pot number you wrote down, and divide by 14. Scale that into each container. Every bowl comes in around 871 calories with 60 grams of protein.

head.description: Copycat chicken scampi meal prep with garlic butter sauce and peppers. 14 bowls at 871 calories and 60g protein each, about $4.03 a serving (at everyday cost).
head.keywords: chicken scampi, olive garden copycat, garlic butter pasta, budget meal prep, high protein pasta, cheap dinner recipes
recipeIngredient: 2 lemons worth of lemon juice (105 g)
steps: Boil spaghetti just short of done and toss with a little oil.
Flour-dredge chicken strips and sear to 165 F; saute the peppers and onions.
Make the sauce: butter, garlic, and red pepper flakes, a little flour, then whisk in broth and lemon juice until it thickens.
Toss chicken, vegetables, and spaghetti in the sauce with half the parmesan.
Portion into 14 containers and finish with the remaining parmesan.
